quote: Live not for battles won. / Live not for the-end-of-the-song. / Live in the along.
source: Gwendolyn Brooks, Speech to the Young: Speech to the Progress-Toward, Family Pictures (1970), closing lines

evidence.where: Poetry Society of America, Poetry in Motion page, fetched this run, which credits Blacks (Third World Press, 1991); first publication in Family Pictures (Broadside Press, 1970) confirmed by secondary sources in search
evidence.edition: Blacks (Chicago: Third World Press, 1991); first in Family Pictures (Detroit: Broadside Press, 1970)
evidence.locator: last three lines of the poem

reason: The Poetry Society of America prints the three closing lines exactly as proposed, hyphens included, from Blacks. The proposal’s claim that it is the last poem in Family Pictures was not confirmed this run, so the source line does not assert it. Brooks has one line in the year (February), none in March; not shipped.
